claims.claim: From 2025, a closely held company (held by no more than five individuals) with business profitability above 25% has the excess attributed to its active shareholders and taxed at their marginal rates
claims.raw_snippet: As of 2025, when the profitability (defined as taxable income divided by revenue) of a closely held company ( as defined above ) from business activity (i.e. income from any source other than interest, dividends, rent, consideration for the sale of assets, income from securities that constitute business inventory, consideration from the sale of real estate in Israel or abroad, or the shares of real estate companies) exceeds 25%, an active shareholder's (defined as a shareholder holding 30% or more of at least one of the means of control of the closely held company or a shareholder holding less than 30% thereof who is involved in generating the business income of the closely held company or involved in the management of the closely held company) pro-rata share of the income constituting the excess profitability (i.e. exceeding 25%) is included in the active shareholder's taxable income and subject to tax at the active shareholder's marginal tax rate.

claims.claim: As of 2025, 45% of Israeli tech startups are incorporated abroad, up from 20% in 2022
claims.raw_snippet: as of 2025, 45% of Israeli tech startups are incorporated abroad , more than double the share just three years ago. The move is not only about legal convenience; it reflects a combination of investor pressure, cost calculations, and, increasingly, a response to political and security uncertainty inside Israel. The war in Gaza has sharpened these pressures. While the tech sector has proven remarkably resilient — raising billions even amid conflict — entrepreneurs are acutely aware of the optics of risk. Many foreign investors still love Israeli innovation but prefer to see it wrapped in the legal safety of Delaware, Nevada, or even London. For founders, this creates a profound dilemma: protect their local brand and ecosystem, or adapt to international norms and expectations in order to survive and grow. How this balance is struck in the coming years will determine not just the fate of individual companies but also the long-term positioning of Israel as a hub of global innovation. A Dramatic Shift in Incorporation Habits The IATI survey, conducted in mid-2025, found that nearly half of all new Israeli startups are incorporated outside of Israel . Only a few years earlier, in 2022, that number was just 20%
